Definition: from ἀλαλή (a shout, "halloo"); to vociferate, i.e. (by implication) to wail; figuratively, to clang:--tinkle, wail.
BiblicalUsage: Twice, and the two uses could hardly be further apart. In Corinth it is the clanging cymbal, a loud noise with no love behind it, which is what a gifted tongue becomes without love. In Capernaum it is the wailing at Jairus's house, the hired mourners making a tumult around a dead girl before Jesus takes her by the hand.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for making a loud noise carries no theology of its own; its weight is the contrast, that noise without love is nothing and grief without hope is answered by a word from Christ.
